did: Split docs/calls.json into docs/calls/<ID>.json, one file per call: 161 files generated by script and checked by a round trip, key order included, then prettier-formatted. The old file is deleted. Added one loader, packages/eslint/src/calls-record.ts (exported as @some-ui/eslint-kit/calls). It reads the working tree or any commit, and reads a commit from before the split as the old array. check:calls, check:commit-trailers, render call-facts and the interview week's monday all read through it. check:calls now also refuses a file not named for its call, anything in the folder other than C<n>.json, and docs/calls.json reappearing. Its ratchet holds against a base in either layout. In the folder, moves may name any other call in the record. render call-facts lists a week read from the folder by (made, id); a week read from the old array keeps its order. Weeks before the split stay byte-identical, and so does the Monday bundle. The before/after order for the week that crosses the split is in the PR body. History holds: the old reader and the new loader agree at every commit of origin/main~150..main. Three independent reviews are recorded on #2992. Their findings are fixed or answered. git-tree.ts gained readBlobs (one batched cat-file), which readFilesAt now shares.
left: eslint-kit is now a runtime dependency of video-render and interview-week, because their lint requires it for cli.ts and scripts/monday.ts. That puts eslint-kit in www's build graph; it costs build time only.
In the folder layout, two calls can now move each other. Nothing follows moves chains, so it is harmless.
